A.description: Angle of a taper in a thread cycle, written instead of the taper amount.
A.label: Taper angle

B.description: Angle at which a thread cycle feeds in along the flank, usually the angle of the insert tip.
B.label: Infeed angle

C.description: Angle of the spindle while it works as the C axis, used to place holes and flats for driven tools. In a thread cycle it sets the start angle of the thread instead.
C.label: C axis

D.description: Depth the cycle takes per pass or per peck.
D.label: Depth of cut or peck

DA.description: How far a grooving or drilling cycle retracts after each peck. It is always written with an equals sign; without it the control uses its own setting.
DA.label: Pull-back after each peck

E.description: Time the tool waits at the bottom of a cycle, counted like the time of G04. In a variable-lead thread it is the change of lead per turn instead, and in a LAP shape it is the feed the roughing cycle uses along that part of the shape.
E.label: Dwell, lead change or shape feed

F.description: Feed rate; the unit follows the feed mode, distance per minute with G94 and per spindle revolution with G95. With G04 it is the dwell time, and in a thread block it is the lead.
F.label: Feed, dwell time or thread lead

G.description: Selects how the control reads the rest of the block: the kind of movement, the cycle, the feed mode and the measuring modes.
G.label: Preparatory function

H.description: Height of the thread profile, written as a diameter, in the multi-pass thread cycles.
H.label: Thread height

I.description: Distance from the start point to the arc centre across the turning axis, signed and always incremental. In the cycles it is a taper, a shift between passes or an approach distance instead.
I.label: Arc centre on X, or a shift

J.description: How many threads share the lead written in F. It is a count.
J.label: Threads within the lead

K.description: Distance from the start point to the arc centre along the turning axis, signed and always incremental. In the cycles it is a taper, a shift between passes or an approach distance instead.
K.label: Arc centre on Z, or a shift

L.description: Radius of an arc, written instead of I and K; this control does not take R for it. In the other blocks it is the size of a chamfer or a corner round, the chamfer at the end of a thread, or the relief of a deep-hole cycle.
L.label: Arc radius, chamfer or relief

M.description: Switches a machine function such as the spindle, the coolant or the gear range. Numbers this database does not describe are set up by the machine builder and are not errors.
M.label: Machine function

N.description: Name of the block: digits, or a name that starts with a letter, up to four characters. A space has to follow it, and leading zeros count, so N0123 and N123 are two names.
N.label: Sequence number or name

O.description: Name of the program, up to four characters. Names are compared as text, so O0123 and O123 are two different programs.
O.label: Program name

P.description: Synchronization code between the two turrets of a two-turret machine.
P.label: Turret synchronization code

Q.description: How often a subprogram call repeats, how many evenly spaced holes a driven-tool cycle makes, or how many starts a thread has. It is a count and never a length.
Q.label: Repeat or hole count

R.description: How far a driven-tool drilling or tapping cycle feeds in from its cutting start. The sign gives the direction, and along X it is a diameter.
R.label: Infeed of a driven-tool cycle

S.description: Spindle speed in revolutions per minute, or the cutting speed while G96 is active. With G50 it is the speed the control may not exceed. The unit system of the machine does not change it.
S.label: Spindle speed

SA.description: Speed of the C axis in the driven-tool thread cycles G185 to G188. It is always written with an equals sign.
SA.label: C-axis speed in a driven-tool thread

SB.description: Speed of the driven-tool spindle, not of the main spindle. It is always written with an equals sign, in the block of M13 or M14 or before it.
SB.label: Driven-tool speed

T.description: Four digits are the station and the offset number; six digits put the nose radius compensation number in front of them, so T020305 is station 03 with offset 05. The turret indexes before the axes of the same block move.
T.label: Turret station, offset and nose radius

U.description: Material left on the diameter for the finishing pass. It is an allowance, not an incremental move: this control writes incremental moves with G91.
U.label: Finish allowance on X

W.description: Material left along the turning axis for the finishing pass. It is an allowance, not an incremental move.
W.label: Finish allowance on Z

X.description: Position across the turning axis, written as a diameter. It stays a diameter in incremental mode (G91).
X.label: X axis, a diameter

Y.description: Position across the turning axis on machines that have a Y axis.
Y.label: Y axis

codes.description: Moves to the position at rapid speed. Every axis goes at its own rapid rate instead of in step with the others, so the tool can leave the straight line between start and end.
codes.label: Rapid

codes.description: Moves to the position on a straight line at the feed in F.
codes.label: Linear feed move

codes.description: Cuts an arc clockwise in the turning plane. The centre is given by I and K, or the radius by L; with L both X and Z are needed and I and K may not stand in the block.
codes.label: Arc, clockwise

params.label: Centre across the turning axis, from the start point
Centre along Z, from the start point
Radius, written instead of I and K

codes.description: Cuts an arc counter-clockwise in the turning plane. The centre is given by I and K, or the radius by L; with L both X and Z are needed and I and K may not stand in the block.
codes.label: Arc, counter-clockwise

params.label: Centre across the turning axis, from the start point
Centre along Z, from the start point
Radius, written instead of I and K

codes.description: Holds the position for the time in F before the next block runs. F is a time here and not a feed, so nothing that scales feeds may touch it; the machine's unit system decides what one unit of it is.
codes.label: Dwell

codes.description: On a machine with two turrets, the blocks that follow are for turret A.
codes.label: Turret A

codes.description: On a machine with two turrets, the blocks that follow are for turret B.
codes.label: Turret B
Compensation plane XY, for driven-tool milling on the face

codes.description: In force at power-on and after a reset, and selected again by M109.
codes.label: Compensation plane ZX, the turning plane
Compensation plane YZ, for driven-tool milling on the side

codes.description: Moves to the home position. It is not the inch switch it is on other controls.
codes.label: Home position return

codes.description: Moves to the home position for a tool change. It is not the metric switch it is on other controls.
codes.label: Tool-change home position return

codes.description: Cuts one threading pass to the diameter in X, written the same way as G33. A following block with only a new X cuts the next pass. F is the lead of the thread, never a feed rate.
codes.label: Thread pass along Z

params.label: Taper, as the difference in radius from start to end
Taper angle, written instead of I
Chamfer at the end of the thread, with M23

codes.description: Cuts one threading pass across the face to the X in the block, at the Z of the pass; the lead runs along X. F is the lead of the thread, never a feed rate.
codes.label: Face thread pass

params.label: Taper, as the difference from start to end
Taper angle, written instead of K
Chamfer at the end of the thread, with M23

codes.description: Cuts one threading pass to the diameter in X and ends at Z. A following block with only a new X cuts the next pass, which is how a post writes a list of passes. F is the lead of the thread, never a feed rate.
codes.label: Thread pass along Z

params.label: Taper, as the difference in radius from start to end
Taper angle, written instead of I
Chamfer at the end of the thread, with M23

codes.description: Cuts a thread whose lead grows by E every turn, starting from the lead in F. Neither F nor E is a feed rate.
codes.label: Variable-lead thread, lead growing

params.label: Change of the lead per turn

codes.description: Cuts a thread whose lead shrinks by E every turn, starting from the lead in F. Neither F nor E is a feed rate.
codes.label: Variable-lead thread, lead shrinking

params.label: Change of the lead per turn

codes.description: Moves the feed axis in step with the turn of the driven-tool spindle. The feed is tied to that spindle like the pitch of a tap, so it may never be scaled on its own.
codes.label: Feed in step with the driven tool, forward

codes.description: Moves the feed axis in step with the driven-tool spindle turning the other way. The feed is tied to that spindle like the pitch of a tap, so it may never be scaled on its own.
codes.label: Feed in step with the driven tool, reverse

codes.description: Offsets the path by the nose radius, with the tool on the left of the part seen along the direction of travel. The radius comes from the nose radius number of the six-digit T word.
codes.label: Nose radius compensation, tool left

codes.description: Offsets the path by the nose radius, with the tool on the right of the part seen along the direction of travel. The radius comes from the nose radius number of the six-digit T word.
codes.label: Nose radius compensation, tool right

codes.description: With S it is the highest speed the spindle may reach, which a program sets before it turns the constant cutting speed on; the limit holds until another one is set. With X or Z it shifts the zero point for the blocks that follow instead, and no T word may stand in that block.
codes.label: Spindle speed limit, or zero shift

params.label: New X value of the present position, for a zero shift
New Z value of the present position, for a zero shift

codes.description: Each move hands over to the next without waiting for the axes to catch up, so a sharp corner comes out slightly rounded.
codes.label: Corner droop control off

codes.description: The control lets each corner settle before the next move starts, so the path keeps sharp corners.
codes.label: Corner droop control on

codes.description: Cuts a whole thread in passes from one block; B, D and the M codes of the block decide the infeed, and U leaves an allowance for the last pass. It is a thread cycle on this control and not a roughing cycle. F is the lead, never a feed rate.
codes.label: Multi-pass thread cycle along Z

params.label: Taper, as the difference in radius from start to end
Taper angle, written instead of I
Depth of the first cut, as a diameter
Allowance for the last pass, as a diameter
Chamfer at the end of the thread, with M23
Change of the lead per turn, for a variable-lead thread

codes.description: Cuts a whole face thread in passes from one block; B, D and the M codes of the block decide the infeed, and W leaves an allowance for the last pass. F is the lead, never a feed rate.
codes.label: Multi-pass thread cycle on the face

params.label: Taper, as the difference from start to end
Taper angle, written instead of K
Chamfer at the end of the thread, with M23
Change of the lead per turn, for a variable-lead thread

codes.description: Cuts grooves in pecks along X and shifts by K along Z between them. A T word in the block only changes the offset used at the end point; it is not a tool change.
codes.label: Grooving cycle, infeed along X

params.label: Position of the last groove along Z
Shift along X, as a diameter
Shift along Z between the grooves
Depth after which the tool pulls fully out, as a diameter
Offset for the end point; not a tool change

codes.description: Grooves into the face in pecks, or drills a hole in pecks with X at zero. A T word in the block only changes the offset used at the end point; it is not a tool change.
codes.label: Face grooving or peck drilling

params.label: Groove position, as a diameter; X0 drills on centre
Shift along X between the grooves, as a diameter
Depth after which the tool pulls fully out
Offset for the end point; not a tool change

codes.description: Adds a chamfer of size L at the end of the G01 move in the same block, which may carry only one of X and Z. It is not a grooving cycle as on other controls.
codes.label: Chamfer at the end of a G01 move

codes.description: Adds a round of radius L at the end of the G01 move in the same block, which may carry only one of X and Z. It is not a threading cycle here, but the same number cuts a thread on other lathe controls, so gEdit will not scale the F of such a block: a feed left alone costs one edit by hand, a scaled thread lead scraps the part.
codes.label: Corner round at the end of a G01 move

codes.description: Taps along Z from one block and reverses the spindle at the bottom; the spindle speed has to be set before it. The feed carries the pitch, so it may never be scaled.
codes.label: Tapping cycle, right-hand

params.label: Rapid approach before the tap starts cutting
Tapping feed, tied to the pitch

codes.description: Taps a left-hand thread along Z from one block and reverses the spindle at the bottom; the spindle speed has to be set before it. The feed carries the pitch, so it may never be scaled.
codes.label: Tapping cycle, left-hand

params.label: Rapid approach before the tap starts cutting
Tapping feed, tied to the pitch

codes.description: Ends the shape definition that G81, G82 or G83 started. It does not cancel a drilling cycle as on other controls.
codes.label: End of a LAP shape

codes.description: Starts the definition of the finished shape for automatic roughing along Z. Its block carries the sequence name the LAP call refers to. It is not a drilling cycle.
codes.label: Start of a LAP shape along Z

codes.description: Starts the definition of the finished shape for automatic roughing across the face. It is not a drilling cycle.
codes.label: Start of a LAP shape on the face

codes.description: Starts the definition of the blank for automatic roughing. It is not a drilling cycle.
codes.label: Start of the LAP blank shape

codes.description: Gives a LAP roughing cycle a new depth of cut and a new feed part-way through. It stands on a line that starts with $ and continues the G85 block: from the point XA= (ZA= on the face) the cycle cuts with DA= and FA=, and from XB= (ZB=) with DB= and FB=. The same number is a tapping cycle on other lathe controls and on the machining centres, so gEdit scales neither the F of such a block nor the spindle speed it runs at.
codes.label: New depth and feed within LAP roughing

params.label: First change point, as a diameter
First change point along Z, on the face
Depth of cut after the first point
Second change point, as a diameter
Second change point along Z, on the face
Depth of cut after the second point

codes.description: Roughs along the shape whose sequence name follows the code, leaving U and W for finishing. No S, T or M word may stand in the block, and a change of cutting conditions (G84) goes on the lines after it that start with $.
codes.label: LAP roughing

params.label: Finish allowance on X, as a diameter

codes.description: Roughs by copying the shape whose sequence name follows the code, which suits a cast or forged blank. No S, T or M word may stand in the block.
codes.label: LAP copy roughing

params.label: Roughing feed, until the shape sets one with E
Finish allowance on X, as a diameter

codes.description: Finishes along the shape whose sequence name follows the code, at the feeds the shape itself writes. No S, T or M word may stand in the block.
codes.label: LAP finishing

params.label: Allowance left on X, as a diameter

codes.description: Cuts a thread along the shape whose sequence name follows the code; the leads are written in that shape. The same number is a tapping cycle on other lathe controls, so gEdit scales neither the F of such a block nor the spindle speed it runs at.
codes.label: LAP continuous threading

codes.description: Positions are distances from the zero point; this is the state after a reset. X stays a diameter.
codes.label: Absolute positions

codes.description: Positions are distances from the point before, and X is still written as a diameter. G90 and G91 may not stand in the same block.
codes.label: Incremental positions

codes.description: This control gives G92 no function. On lathe controls of other makes the same number cuts thread passes, and a program written for one of them may have been opened with this dialect, so gEdit will not scale the F of such a block.
codes.label: Not assigned on this control

codes.description: F is a distance per minute from here on. The driven-tool drilling and tapping cycles need it.
codes.label: Feed per minute

codes.description: F is a distance per spindle revolution from here on; this is the state after a reset.
codes.label: Feed per revolution

codes.description: S is a cutting speed from here on, and the control changes the spindle speed with the diameter. The block needs an S word, a speed limit should be set with G50 before it, and no thread may be cut while it is on.
codes.label: Constant cutting speed

codes.description: S is a speed in revolutions per minute from here on. The block needs an S word.
codes.label: Fixed spindle speed

codes.description: Taps with the feed tied to the spindle turn, so the feed carries the pitch and may never be scaled.
codes.label: Synchronized tapping, right-hand

codes.description: Taps a left-hand thread with the feed tied to the spindle turn, so the feed carries the pitch and may never be scaled.
codes.label: Synchronized tapping, left-hand

codes.description: On a machine with two turrets, the constant cutting speed of G96 is kept for the tool of turret A; G110 brings it back there after G111.
codes.label: Constant cutting speed follows turret A

codes.description: On a machine with two turrets, the constant cutting speed of G96 is kept for the tool of turret B instead of turret A, until G110.
codes.label: Constant cutting speed follows turret B

codes.description: Cuts a thread along a clockwise arc, for example in the shape of a LAP thread. The arc is given by a centre in I and K or a radius in L. F is the lead, never a feed rate, and E changes it per thread.
codes.label: Thread along an arc, clockwise

codes.description: Cuts a thread along a counter-clockwise arc, for example in the shape of a LAP thread. The arc is given by a centre in I and K or a radius in L. F is the lead, never a feed rate, and E changes it per thread.
codes.label: Thread along an arc, counter-clockwise

codes.description: Ends G137 and G138: X is a diameter again. It stands in a block of its own.
codes.label: Coordinate conversion and Y-axis mode off

codes.description: Machines the face in Cartesian X and Y instead of X and C: the C of the block gives the direction of the new X axis, and from here on X and Y are radius values until G136.
codes.label: Coordinate conversion on

codes.description: X, Y and Z are programmed as a Cartesian system, X as a radius, until G136. The mode survives a reset, so a post writes G136 or G138 before the first move of a tool.
codes.label: Y-axis mode on

codes.description: The blocks that follow machine a part held in the main spindle, in its program coordinate system and with its zero offset. It stands at the start of a program, or right after G13 or G14.
codes.label: Machining with the main spindle

codes.description: The blocks that follow machine a part held in the sub spindle, in its own program coordinate system and with its own zero offset, whose Z runs the other way. Speeds and M codes are written as for the main spindle, so a plain S there may not be the main spindle's.
codes.label: Machining with the sub spindle

codes.description: The blocks that follow machine a part held in the pick-off spindle, so a spindle speed there may not be the main spindle's.
codes.label: Machining with the pick-off spindle
Machining with the pick-off spindle and the third turret

codes.description: Taps with the driven tool, its turn tied to the feed, until G180 cancels it. The feed carries the pitch, so it may never be scaled.
codes.label: Driven-tool synchronized tapping, forward

codes.description: Taps a left-hand thread with the driven tool, its turn tied to the feed, until G180 cancels it. The feed carries the pitch, so it may never be scaled.
codes.label: Driven-tool synchronized tapping, reverse

codes.description: Ends the driven-tool cycle that is active. It stands in a block of its own, and the block after it has to move both X and Z.
codes.label: Cancel the driven-tool cycle

codes.description: Drills with the driven tool at the position of this block and of every following block that names a new position, until G180. The feed is per minute (G94), and Q drills that many holes spaced evenly around C.
codes.label: Driven-tool drilling

codes.description: Changes the tool on a machine with a tool changer. A turret indexes on the T word alone and needs no M6.

codes.description: The thread cycles pull out with a chamfer at the end of the thread, as long as the L of the cycle.
codes.label: Thread chamfer on

codes.description: A variable-lead thread (G34, G35) takes its lead along Z; that is what the control assumes without M26 or M27.

codes.description: A variable-lead thread (G34, G35) takes its lead along X, for a thread on the face.

codes.description: Under constant cutting speed the next move starts without waiting for the spindle to reach its speed.

codes.description: The tailstock quill presses with its lower force. It is not a subprogram call as on other controls; that is CALL here.

codes.description: The tailstock quill presses with its higher force. It does not end a subprogram as on other controls; that is RTS here.

codes.description: Returns the spindle from C-axis positioning to turning.
codes.label: C-axis mode off

codes.description: Couples the C axis to the spindle so it can be positioned for driven tools. It has to stand alone in its block.

codes.description: Ends a subprogram and goes on after the block that called it.

codes.description: Continues at the block with that sequence name, in the same program.
